headline: Saudi Oil Exports Reach Five-Month High While Output Drops to Record Low
summary: Saudi Arabia's crude exports rose 7.9% in August to 4.451 million barrels per day, reaching their highest level since March, even as crude production fell to a record low of 6.24 million bpd.
why: Saudi Arabia is the world's largest crude exporter and leader of OPEC, making its production quotas and export volumes pivotal for global oil balances.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Lower production curbs baseline global supply, but higher seaborne exports increase near-term spot market availability.

why_moved: Crude benchmarks balanced the conflicting signals of a multi-month peak in Saudi seaborne shipments against a record decline in domestic crude output.
